review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the ThreeGap directory for simp attributes and for coordinate or apply lemmas about astar, aprt and rem. I found none. The file has no simp annotations. Its proofs unfold the vector-literal definitions `astar` and `aprt` with `simp only` lists that are repeated by hand. Two further patterns looked suspect: the long `interval_cases` blocks and the `nine_le_card_image` chain. I did not report them because they are not simp-interface issues. I did not run Lean, so I claim nothing about simp behaviour that I observed.

findings.problem: `astar` and `aprt` are vector-literal definitions with no coordinate lemmas, so there is no canonical normal form for `astar 0`, `astar 1`, `astar 2`, `aprt s 0` and so on. Every proof therefore unfolds the definition and then spells out the `Matrix.cons_val_*` rules by hand. The coordinate-2 case also needs `Matrix.head_cons` and `Matrix.tail_cons`. Examples are c0/c1/c2 in `delta_astar` (lines 71–78), e0/e1/e2 in `norm_aprt` (lines 597–602) and the same three in `norm_aprt'` (lines 616–621). The same unfolding-plus-simp-set pattern recurs about eight times, and each copy mixes unfolding with arithmetic normalisation.
findings.proposed_change: Add coordinate lemmas directly after the definitions, for example `@[simp] theorem astar_zero : astar 0 = -785 / 50000 := rfl`, with matching `astar_one` and `astar_two`. Add `aprt_zero`, `aprt_one` and `aprt_two` in the same way. The `rfl` proofs are untested. If `rfl` fails, use `by simp [astar]`. Optionally make `astar` and `aprt` irreducible for simp, so the proofs rewrite with these lemmas instead of unfolding. After that, c0/c1/c2 and e0/e1/e2 reduce to `simp [rem, astar_zero]` followed by `push_cast; ring`, or to plain `simp` followed by `ring`.
findings.benefit: Readers get one stable normal form for the coordinates, and no proof has to remember which `Matrix.cons_val_*`, `head_cons` and `tail_cons` rules the third coordinate needs. Changing a witness constant no longer touches every proof. Downstream files can also simp with these lemmas.

findings.excerpt: intro p; simp only [rem, astar, Pi.sub_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Matrix.cons_val_zero]
findings.problem: `rem` is a plain def, `(q : ℝ) • α - (fun k => (p k : ℝ))`. The ThreeGap files I grepped contain no `rem_apply` coordinate lemma and no `@[simp]` lemma for it. Each coordinate proof has to unfold `rem` and then list `Pi.sub_apply`, `Pi.smul_apply` and `smul_eq_mul` by hand. This file repeats that three times in `delta_astar`, and any other user of `rem` must do the same.
findings.proposed_change: In SimultaneousApprox.lean, next to `rem`, add `@[simp] theorem rem_apply (α : Fin n → ℝ) (q : ℤ) (p : Fin n → ℤ) (k : Fin n) : rem α q p k = (q : ℝ) * α k - (p k : ℝ)`. It should be provable by `simp [rem]`, though I have not tested that. Then c0/c1/c2 in `delta_astar` become `simp [astar_zero]; push_cast; ring`, or something close to that.
findings.benefit: The unfolding and coordinate-evaluation rules are stated once in a simp lemma on `rem` instead of being repeated in each proof. The normal form `rem α q p k = q * α k - p k` is easy for readers to find. Every proof that evaluates `rem` at a coordinate gets shorter and no longer depends on the exact definition of `rem`.
